source: ai_results.py (T-048); every value below is read from the tables named in "source"
blanket: This is AI-based research. Numbers are measured on this collection, with 95 % intervals where a sample was drawn.

methods.label: Find look-alikes in other museums
methods.line: For one object, list the most similar-looking objects held by other museums, from the photograph alone.

headline.what: of the ten nearest objects from other museums share the query's catalogue category
headline.n_what: objects with a coarse catalogue category

methods.caveat: The target is the museum's own coarse category (six classes), which is a catalogue word, not an expert judgement. Catalogue words alone score higher (0.870) but that test is circular, because the category is itself taken from the words.

examples.rule: Seed 20261119 draws 40 objects with a category and a photograph; the first three that have neighbours in other museums are shown, then the first later draw with a miss. Neighbours shown are the stored closest ones from other museums (up to three).

draw.note: a small illustration, not an estimate: the estimate is the headline number above

methods.source: ai-deep/summary.json method_evidence (photo, shape, multimodal); ai-deep/experiments.json finding F1

methods.label: Group objects across museums
methods.line: Sort the whole collection into groups by look alone, then count which museums each group reaches. The museum is never an input.

headline.what: median purity: the share of a group that belongs to its most common device family
headline.spread: 57 of the 162 groups reach two or more museums; 132 pass the purity line of 0.30
headline.n_what: look-groups of at least 40 objects, covering 31,945 objects (57.0 % of the collection)
headline.baseline_note: No random-grouping baseline was run for the look groups. Purity is measured against the device-family codebook labels (T-030), which are themselves assigned by a model.

methods.caveat: 30 of 162 groups are mixed (purity below 0.30) and are named "Mixed group". 24,128 objects (43.0 %) are in no look-group: they have no usable photograph or too few close neighbours.

examples.rule: The look-group that reaches the most museums and passes purity (a clean one), and the largest mixed group (a failure), each with one photograph per museum (up to four).

methods.label: Search the collection in plain words
methods.line: Type what you want in English, Dutch or Swedish; the model returns photographs, without any catalogue keyword match.

headline.what: of the top 20 photographs are the right kind of object (mean of 18 queries)
headline.ci_note: t-interval (17 degrees of freedom) over the 18 per-query values, derived here

methods.caveat: A hit means the photograph's catalogue category matches the query's expected category. Photographs with no category are shown as unscored, not as wrong. 18 queries is a small set.

examples.rule: Seed 20261120 picks one English, one Dutch and one Swedish query from the 18 scored ones, plus the query with the lowest precision. First five hits of each.

methods.source: ai-deep/crossmodal.json; ai-deep/tasks.json (per-query precision and hits); ai-deep/experiments.json finding F10

methods.label: Suggest what an object was used for
methods.line: Combine the catalogue wording with what the photograph and outline neighbours suggest, and say where the two agree, disagree or are silent.

headline.what: of the 3,005 catalogue-rule function statements are independently supported by the image neighbours
headline.n_what: object-function pairs where a catalogue rule asserts a use (all 2,830 records, 8 functions: a census, not a sample)
headline.spread: calibration on held-out groups: expected calibration error at most 0.051
headline.baseline_note: No baseline and no expert truth exist for function: this is agreement between two weak sources (catalogue rules and image neighbours), not accuracy.

methods.caveat: No expert-checked function labels exist. "Supported" means the image neighbours agree with the catalogue rules, which are themselves derived from catalogue text; agreement is not correctness of use.

examples.rule: Seed 20261121 draws two supported pairs and one image-only suggestion at random; the wrong one is chosen on purpose: the first "dental forceps" for which the image neighbours contradict the catalogue use "extraction".

methods.source: ai-deep/experiments.json hypotheses.state_counts and hypotheses.calibration; finding F9

methods.label: Flag objects that may contain asbestos
methods.line: From an object's function and the museum's inspection materials, call it as containing asbestos or not, to decide what to sample first.

headline.what: of the 88 objects the museum tested were called correctly (62)
headline.n_what: tested objects: 42 contained asbestos, 46 did not
headline.spread: flags 26 of 42 containing objects, clears 36 of 46 clean ones

methods.caveat: The museum chose which objects to test, so this is not the rate in the collection. Out-of-fold predictions; 88 objects is a small set.

examples.rule: Seed 20261122 picks one object of each outcome (contains and flagged, clean and cleared, contains and missed, clean and flagged) among the tested objects that have a photograph.

not_worked.claim: Deep models on the bare outline do no better than the hand-made outline distance.
not_worked.evidence: Cross-museum P@10 difference vs outline: DINOv2-L silhouette +0.006 [-0.004, 0.017]; DINOv2-B +0.005 [-0.005, 0.016]; SigLIP 2 +0.013 [0.003, 0.024]; CLIP -0.014 [-0.025, -0.004].

not_worked.claim: Cropping the working ends is worse than using the whole object for fine subtypes.
not_worked.evidence: Fine-subtype P@10 (31 subtypes, 988 records): ends minus whole -0.073 [-0.087, -0.059]; whole+ends minus whole +0.013 [0.006, 0.020]; within the same coarse category +0.007 [-0.000, 0.014].

not_worked.claim: Words-only prompts say little about what an object was used for.
not_worked.evidence: Affordance prompts vs weak function labels: mAP 0.39 (SigLIP 2 raw) vs prevalence 0.19, against 0.91 for image-neighbour transfer; extraction and scraping near chance.

not_worked.claim: The model trained to ignore museum photography equals, but does not beat, the larger frozen model on an unseen museum.
not_worked.evidence: Unseen Region Skane (model never saw it): cross-museum P@10 +0.046 vs frozen DINOv2-B (seed range 0.041-0.051; seed-17 CI [0.029, 0.062]); +0.003 vs frozen DINOv2-L (seed-17 CI [-0.011, 0.019]).

not_worked.claim: Photo embeddings carry which museum took the picture.
not_worked.evidence: Background green channel R^2 from DINOv2-L raw 0.83; from the silhouette view 0.05.

not_worked.claim: On outside photographs the family is right 73.4 % of the time (95 % CI 70.4 to 76.2), against 55.8 % for always guessing the commonest family; for historical photographs balanced accuracy is 0.55.
not_worked.evidence: Raw view: balanced accuracy 0.61, macro-F1 0.60 (chance 0.25; majority accuracy 0.56; n = 1,248 external photographs).

not_worked.claim: Catalogue words alone almost never flag a containing object, and they are the only model usable on an untested object.
not_worked.evidence: At p >= 0.5 the catalogue-words model flags 5 of 42 containing objects and clears 45 of 46 clean ones (results/tables/asbestos_ai.json, decision).

not_worked.claim: Similarity is not descent: nothing here separates inherited design from convergent design.
not_worked.evidence: None of these representations can distinguish inherited design from convergent solutions to the same mechanical problem. Neighbour structure is a candidate generator for comparisons that must then be tested with dated, documented maker/designer links and coded characters.

abstain.line: On 19,481 of the 22,640 object-function pairs the function view abstains: the evidence is insufficient, which is not a "no".
